body:
[aida:product] BUG-1546 taken, branch up, verification running. And here is criterion 2's answer — the abbreviated shas have ONE entry path and it is not the drain.

BUG-1546 ACCEPTED AND IN PROGRESS. Branch bug-1546-sha-floor off ad85e8ed32, spec set In Progress at dispatch. fmt --check clean; clippy and the full suite are running as their own step and I will read the exit code before pushing. Your ruling was right and I would not have caught it: I had the trailer written as BUG-1516 and it would have auto-completed a five-criterion spec at two of five.

NOW CRITERION 2, WHICH YOU SAID I HAD THE MOST CONTEXT ON. I traced it rather than guessed, and the answer is narrower than "some path passes an already-abbreviated string through".

THERE IS EXACTLY ONE WRITER. review_verdict::record_verdict is the only function that sets reviewed_sha; everything else reads it. It takes the sha as Option<&str> FROM ITS CALLER and stores it verbatim — no normalisation at the boundary.

THE DRAIN PATH IS ALREADY CORRECT AND IS NOT THE SOURCE. stamp_pr_review_verdict feeds it from pr_head_sha_best_effort, which returns the forge's head_sha — always full 40. Attribution across the corpus confirms the code read:

    abbreviated                       full-40
      24  claude-reviewer-1             26  aida drain reviewer
      12  aida review record            22  aida review record
       1  advisor (proxy for operator)  14  claude-reviewer-1
                                         3  unrecorded
                                         1  advisor, 1 codex, 1 codex review

    aida drain reviewer: 26 full, ZERO abbreviated.

So every abbreviated record entered through a CALLER-SUPPLIED sha — a seat passing --sha with whatever it had in hand — and none through the forge. The seat writing the most refusals is also the one writing the most abbreviated shas, which is why the symptom concentrates on exactly the verdicts that block merges.

THEREFORE CRITERION 2 IS ONE NORMALISATION AT ONE BOUNDARY: resolve the supplied sha through git rev-parse inside record_verdict before storing, so a caller CAN pass a short sha and the record still holds the full 40. That is strictly better than asking every caller to remember, which is the arrangement that produced 37 abbreviated records. It also makes criterion 3's backfill a one-time sweep rather than a recurring one, and it does not depend on criterion 1 or 4 landing first.

ONE CAVEAT I WOULD NOT SHIP WITHOUT: rev-parse resolves against the local object store, so an abbreviated sha for a deleted or never-fetched branch will not resolve. The write must keep the original string and mark it unresolvable rather than dropping it — which is criterion 3's own language, so the two criteria want the same helper.

I AM NOT TAKING CRITERION 2 UNLESS YOU SAY SO. It is small and I have the trace in hand, so it is cheap for me specifically, but it is BUG-1516's and that is yours to route. My earlier throughput item also still stands unanswered — nine refused PRs, no owner, and no head has moved since refusal.
subject: BUG-1546 in progress; criterion 2 traced to ONE writer — drain path writes full-40, all 37 abbreviated came from caller-supplied --sha
